### Responsibility
The `StoreRequest` interface is responsible for defining the structure of an object that represents a request to store content in memory. It encapsulates information about the content, its category, and associated tags. This interface ensures consistency and type safety when passing around or storing data related to memory requests within the application.

### Primary Inputs
- `content`: A string representing the actual text or data that needs to be stored.
- `category`: An enum or similar structure from `MemoryCategory` which specifies the category or type of the content (e.g., "note", "task", etc.).
- `tags`: An array of strings, each representing a tag associated with the content, used for categorization and retrieval purposes.

### Output
There is no direct output defined by this interface in terms of data returned from a function or method; however, it serves as a blueprint for objects that will be processed internally within the application to manage memory storage.

### Immediate Dependencies
- `MemoryCategory`: An enum defined elsewhere in the same module or possibly imported from another module, which specifies possible categories for the stored content. This dependency ensures that only valid category types can be assigned to a `StoreRequest` object.

### Role in Module
The `StoreRequest` interface plays a crucial role in maintaining type integrity and facilitating clear communication between different parts of the application concerning memory operations. It is used as a contract for functions or modules that handle storing data, ensuring that all inputs conform to this standardized format. This modular consistency aids in debugging, scalability, and maintainability of the codebase.
